nodes.title: Agentic Verification
nodes.value: The running system is judged against what its specs say it is for, by a browser agent that can see and use it safely, so requirements are verified end to end and not only line by line.

claims.text: Validation targets specs that declare a `url:`, accepts a single spec, all specs or one app, resolves relative URLs against a base URL override, and skips with a message a spec that has no URL.

tests.title: scenario 3: spec without url is skipped

claims.text: For each spec the agent perceives the page through a screenshot and an accessibility snapshot, plans a short list of atomic browser actions from the acceptance criteria, performs them and then judges each criterion against the resulting state.

Every acceptance criterion receives exactly one verdict from PASS, FAIL, BLOCKED or INCONCLUSIVE, a FAIL cites its evidence, and a failed LLM call or unavailable evidence yields INCONCLUSIVE rather than a pass.

tests.title: scenario 2: FAIL verdict → exitCode 2
scenario 4: blocked action recorded in results

claims.text: The command exits with the validation-failed code (2) when any criterion or login fails and 0 otherwise, so skipped specs and blocked actions alone do not fail a run.

tests.title: scenario 1: all criteria pass → exitCode 0
scenario 2: FAIL verdict → exitCode 2

claims.text: Screenshots and page evidence are stored per spec under `.specguard/evidence/`, and every run appends an entry with its verdicts and overall result to `.specguard/validation-history.json`.

tests.title: scenario 3: saves screenshot and returns file path
validation history written to .specguard/validation-history.json

claims.text: An optional review step, skipped with `--no-review` or for specs with no UI sections, produces a typed issue report of functional, UX, accessibility and visual problems under `.specguard/reports/`.

Planned actions are classified as safe, destructive or outbound by deterministic whole-word keyword rules, with the real control's role and accessible name taking precedence over the planner's description when the target is known.

tests.title: redacts credentials from login failure error messages

a failed form login redacts credentials from the error

The browser is headless unless configured or `--headed` is passed, runs locally or in Docker as configured, and a missing Playwright installation produces an error with install instructions.

scenario 2: throws PlaywrightUnavailableError when not installed

validation goals are built per capability from its Users & Journeys and Scenarios, so the agent walks real user journeys instead of isolated criteria.
the judge also receives the capability's Problem & Value and returns a capability-level judgement of whether the observed behaviour delivers the stated value, reporting gaps as findings.

tests.title: records PASS and FAIL as agentic proof, matching claim ids exactly, never by substring [agentic-proof]

tests.title: picks up a v2 capability with only a base URL, walks several rounds, and judges value [rounds-and-value]

tests.title: records PASS and FAIL as agentic proof, matching claim ids exactly, never by substring [agentic-proof]
does not let BLOCKED or INCONCLUSIVE overwrite a proof a test run already earned [no-downgrade]

tests.title: replays every step, escapes values, and starts from BASE_URL when set
tags only the passing claims that have an assertion of their own
writes nothing for no steps, and refuses a step whose value the redactor would change
names the file after the capability

claims.text: Page content the model reads (the title, the accessibility tree, the HTML, console errors) and imported or fetched documents are fenced as untrusted data (`<untrusted-...>` tags the content cannot close, a closing tag inside it is defanged), every system message says that nothing inside the fence is an instruction, and what the model proposes is still classified and guarded deterministically, never trusted because it asked

tests.title: wraps text in a labelled fence and says in the system message that the fence holds data

fences the page text and tree the model reads as untrusted data in every step, and tells it so [fenced]

claims.text: One run is bounded: at most five browser steps per round whatever the model plans, `validate.maxRounds` of at most 10, and a wall-clock budget per spec (`validate.timeoutMs`, default 10 minutes) after which no further round is planned, the run says so and judges what it saw

tests.title: takes at most five steps in a round, whatever the model plans [action-cap]
stops planning when the time budget for the spec is spent, and says so, but still judges what it saw [deadline]

claims.text: A check started by an agent (the MCP tool) may target only loopback and the hosts listed in `validate.allowedHosts` (`host`, `host:port` on that port only, `*.domain` for subdomains only); any other target is BLOCKED before a browser or the model sees it; a person on the command line is not restricted

tests.title: allows loopback always, and nothing else unless listed

refuses non-http URLs and text that is not a URL, with a reason
an agent-started run checks loopback and listed hosts only; a person is not restricted [allowlist]

claims.text: The evidence, saved-login and report folders are private to their owner (mode 0700, login files 0600), and `validate.evidenceRetentionDays` removes evidence older than that at the start of a run (default: keep it)

tests.title: removes files older than the retention period, keeps newer ones and the .gitignore marker, and drops emptied folders
keeps the evidence, saved-login and report folders private to their owner [evidence-private]

nodes.title: Conformance Testing
nodes.value: Teams can prove, claim by claim, that the current code delivers what the specs say, and see immediately when a proof is no longer trustworthy.

claims.text: Generation turns every scenario of a spec into one test block titled with the scenario name, importing the module the spec declares, for a single spec or all specs and optionally limited to one app.

tests.title: scenario 1: generates a test from a single spec via --spec
scenario 2: --all processes multiple specs across apps

claims.text: Generation supports unit, integration and end-to-end test types, uses the owning app's framework unless overridden, and uses a browser framework for end-to-end tests in TypeScript.

When a spec has claims, the generation prompt lists each claim with its exact tag and requires it in the verifying test's title, and generation warns about every claim whose tag is missing from the output while still writing the file.

tests.title: lists claims with exact tags in the prompt and warns about missing tags
does not warn when every tag is present

tests.title: scenario 3: skips an existing test file without --force
scenario 4: overwrites an existing test file with --force
scenario 6: strips Markdown fences from LLM output
scenario 7: LLM error records a failure and continues

claims.text: A claim's verdict is failed when any tagged test fails, proven when at least one passes and none fail, and unexercised otherwise, with counts of exercised tests and counterexamples.
The proof ledger stores proven, failed, unexercised and error verdicts; stale is computed and never stored, and unproven means the ledger has no row for the claim.

A proof is stale when the spec (or, for v2 specs, the claim) hash changed, when a source file recorded at ingest changed on disk, or when the repository's dependency fingerprint changed; a file that vanished from the registry alone does not make it stale.

tests.title: marks proofs stale when the spec changes
records the dependency fingerprint and goes stale on a lockfile change
effectiveVerdict ignores a missing fingerprint on either side
goes stale when a recorded source file changes on disk, even before drift runs

claims.text: Each stored row records the claim hash, the source file hashes taken from the spec's declared sources, the dependency fingerprint, the run id, the git revision and the evidence path, so editing one source file stales exactly the claims of the specs that declare it.

tests.title: records the dependency fingerprint and goes stale on a lockfile change
goes stale when a recorded source file changes on disk, even before drift runs

tests.title: runs the configured command and ingests the report in one step [run-and-ingest]

claims.text: A proof records what produced it: a test run leaves `evidence` unset and an agentic browser run records `agentic`
`test generate`, `test run` and `test heal` group the test commands; the older `generate` and `heal` names keep working
After a consolidation, results that still carry old claim tags are accepted for one release through `.specguard/claim-migration.json` and recorded under the new claim refs

Evidence is kept per test layer (`unit`, `integration`, `e2e`, `security`, `functional`): each claim's ledger row holds one entry per layer with its own staleness inputs, and the row's combined fields come from the layer that decides it (a failure in any layer, else the newest proof), so a failing browser check is not overwritten by the next passing unit run and the other way round; a row written before layers existed reads as one layer (`functional` when the browser check wrote it, else `unclassified`) and a project that requires no layers sees exactly the old verdicts

tests.title: reads a row written before layers as one layer, and gives exactly the old verdict when nothing is required
is incomplete, not failed, when a required layer has no proof, and complete once it has
lets a failure in any layer decide, and does not let the next passing layer overwrite it
stales a claim when a required layer goes stale, and ignores a stale layer it does not require
drops superseded unclassified evidence when classified evidence arrives, so an old failure cannot outlive its fix

claims.text: A test's layer is the first of: an `@layer:` tag on the test or a `[layer: x]` comment in the first lines of its file; the app's `test.layers` globs; the suite that ran it; `results ingest --layer`; Playwright means `e2e`; path conventions (`e2e`, `integration`, `security` folders and `.e2e.`/`.int.` file names); otherwise `unit`

nodes.title: Documentation and API
nodes.value: Anyone, human or AI, can read accurate documentation of the system as it is now, pitched at their level, generated from the specs on request and delivered over an API.

claims.text: `docs` rewrites a single spec, all specs or one app's specs into user-facing Markdown pages under `docs/user/` (or a chosen output directory), mirroring the spec's relative path.

tests.title: throws when neither --spec nor --all is provided
scenario 1: generates a doc from a single spec with frontmatter
scenario 2: --all processes multiple specs across apps
scenario 3: custom --out directory

claims.text: Internal-only content (the metadata comment, scenarios and security notes) is removed before the LLM sees the spec, and the rewrite must stay accurate to the supplied spec without inventing features.

tests.title: removes the metadata comment, Scenarios, and Security Notes sections

claims.text: Each generated page starts with frontmatter holding a title, sidebar label, description, category, reading order and a flag marking it as generated.

tests.title: scenario 1: generates a doc from a single spec with frontmatter

claims.text: Generated docs are regenerable artifacts that overwrite existing files, an LLM failure on one spec is recorded and does not stop the others, and the command fails only if every attempted spec failed.

`AGENTS.md` is created from a template when missing and only its marked sections are updated when present, and a failure to generate the section text logs the error and writes nothing.
LLM credentials never appear in any generated page or synchronised section.

claims.text: The traceability matrix and audit data produced by the audit commands are plain JSON or CSV files under `.specguard/` that viewers and auditors can load as documents.

nodes.title: Workspaces - Multi-Repo and Monorepo
nodes.value: Teams that split one system across several repos or packages can treat it as one system, so a change in one place shows what else must be re-checked.

claims.text: A workspace manifest at `.specguard/workspace.json` lists repos with a path and a role of consumer, provider, test or docs, an optional description, and an optional catalog directory; it is found by walking up from any child directory and unknown fields are preserved

A missing manifest is a clear "not found" configuration error and an invalid or schema-failing manifest is a configuration error; repos without their own SpecGuard config load with no config rather than failing

`workspace init` registers sibling repos that have a SpecGuard config, deriving each repo key from the directory name alone and each role from the repo's contents (test frameworks, UI or server dependencies, API schema files, language markers) and never from a platform-specific name; it never overwrites an existing manifest and fails with guidance when no repo is found

claims.text: Monorepo detection reads pnpm, Yarn and npm workspaces, Nx, Turbo and Lerna configuration, expands package globs honouring exclusions, reports the package manager, and records each package's name, directory, test framework and whether it has a test script; a single-package repo is reported as not a monorepo

claims.text: The contract graph is stored in `.specguard/contracts.json` as nodes (a spec in a repo, identified `<repo>::<specPath>`) and directed edges from consumer to provider with a type of graphql, rest, iframe, upload, event, test or docs, a surface list, a last-verified time and a source

`contracts` builds edges from structured contract blocks in spec Dependencies sections, from importers supplied by enabled plugins and, only with `--with-llm`, from free-text dependencies of specs that have no structured block; lines that do not match the format are skipped

Building the graph is idempotent and incremental: existing edges are preserved and surface items merged, `--force` rebuilds from scratch, `--repo <key>` restricts to one repo, validation problems such as an edge naming a missing node are warnings that do not fail the command, and the file is written atomically

`impact` accepts a node id, a workspace-relative path or an absolute path, walks consumers breadth-first to a depth limit (default 6), separates direct from transitive consumers with the connecting edge type and surface, and `--upstream` also lists the providers the target depends on

`impact` suggests a drift command for each affected consumer repo and an "update docs" suggestion for docs-type edges, reports "no downstream consumers" with exit 0, and exits 1 with an example id format for an unresolvable target or with guidance when no graph exists; it never modifies files

`workspace drift` finds repos with changes since a git ref (default the previous commit), maps changed files to graph nodes, runs drift in the affected consumer repos for the dependent specs, supports `--force` and `--repo`, and exits 3 when any consumer has drifted
A claim can be referenced across repos as `repo:specKey#claim` (or `specKey#claim` within the current repo), so a journey or proof can depend on a claim in another repo
